title: Add read-only host check for records-history D111 rules
summary: Add a new athena-core module (part 3 of job 1, D111, design §3) that uses the gh Runner to GET the rulesets view `repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}` for athena/records and main, and reports three rules as in force or not. Audience: Sri, who must set these host rules before the records cutover. Tests use fixture replies; nothing on the host is changed.

defaults_applied.how: Fixture-based unit tests; cargo test and clippy clean.
Reuses existing gh Runner and serde_json.
One new module plus its registration.
Criteria assert reported states from fixtures and GET-only calls.
Doc comments cite D111 and design §3 for outside readers.
Behavior criteria runnable via cargo test/clippy/fmt.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Implemented as a library function in athena-core using the existing gh::Runner trait; no new CLI command is wired unless trivial (not required).
Repo owner/name is passed in by the caller, as with existing gh helpers.
JSON parsing uses serde_json already in the workspace; no new crates.
Rule types per the user: non_fast_forward, deletion, required_status_checks with parameters.strict_required_status_checks_policy true.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: tests feed fixture replies in the rules/branches shape (JSON list of rule objects) and assert: athena/records with a non_fast_forward rule => force-push forbidden in force; a deletion rule => deletion forbidden in force; main with a required_status_checks rule whose parameters.strict_required_status_checks_policy is true => up-to-date required in force.

Tests assert an empty list `[]` reports all rules as not in force, and that a required_status_checks rule with strict_required_status_checks_policy false (or absent) reports up-to-date as not in force; a partial list (only non_fast_forward) reports force-push in force and deletion not in force.

A recording fake Runner test asserts the check issues only GET calls to `repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/athena/records` and `.../rules/branches/main` (not the classic /protection endpoint), with no method override and no field/body arguments, so no host setting changes.
A test where the runner returns an error (e.g. 403 or 5xx) or unparseable JSON asserts the affected rules are reported as unknown/error, not as 'not in force' and not as in force.
The report names each of the three rules and its state in plain text, e.g. 'athena/records: force-push forbidden: in force', so Sri can see which host rule to set.
Doc comments cite D111 and docs/design/records-history.md §3 and describe this as part 3 of job 1; the module is registered in athena-core lib.rs.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test`: all clean and passing for the workspace.

out_of_scope: Changing any host setting, ruleset, or branch protection
Wiring the check into a gate, CLI command, or cutover flow
Other parts/jobs of the records-history plan
